info.description: Design contract only; extends001 without duplicating it. Anonymous endpoints; exact positions require explicit click and tab-RAM consent. Provider-retention disclosure accepted in temporary-processing-v2: Open-Meteo may retain request logs with rounded coordinates up to90days; application logs do not contain coordinates. Runtime notice/consent tests still required. P2 image may be deferred.

requestBody.description: Raw bounded <=5242880 bytes; no multipart spooling, max12MP decoded, no animated/image URL. Entire request no image persistence. P2 disabled503, never pretend enabled.

Point.description: WGS84 point; all exact coordinates only in POST body, not persisted/logged.

scenarioId.description: Required non-null catalog ID only when mode=simulation; null in live. No custom rain values.

PointRequest.description: Server enforces mode/scenario consistency and ST_Covers before outbound work. Consent flag is protocol guard, not authentication.

HistoryRequest.description: Radius immutable from active rule: 1000m inclusive with documented 1mm numerical tolerance. Always real history dataset.

scenarioId.description: Required non-null catalog ID only when mode=simulation; null in live. No custom rain values.

RiskRequest.description: Optional evidenceToken OR manualEvidence, not both; token signed/expiry validated. No user-provided AI score. Evidence only this point.

scenarioId.description: Required non-null catalog ID only when mode=simulation; null in live. No custom rain values.

RouteRequest.description: No arbitrary waypoints/provider URL/profile/rain. v1 uses published car profile, not motorcycle navigation.

WeatherResponse.description: US1 standalone response before risk evaluation; uses shared WeatherSnapshot. Once risk exists, UI rain/chart must use RiskResponse.weatherSnapshot, never a separate or late WeatherResponse.

HistoryResponse.description: Risk facts query all matches, never uses truncated UI page as complete dataset.

RiskValue.description: Missing factors null, uncertainty reserve explicit. Insufficient score/level null. No calibrated real-world safety probability.

RiskResponse.description: Risk and the exact WeatherSnapshot used to compute it are returned together, including insufficient_data results. UI renders rain/chart from this snapshot after risk evaluation; standalone weather responses must not overwrite it, even across cache expiration. No snapshot lookup ID.

weatherSnapshotIndexes.description: Zero-based positions in the containing RouteResponse.weatherSnapshots array for this segment start/mid/end samples. Every index must be in bounds; payload-local positions, not persisted/server lookup IDs.

weatherSnapshots.description: Full values actually used for returned routes; segment weatherSnapshotIndexes address this response array only, never a server-side snapshot store.

RouteResponse.description: 1-3 candidates, not globally optimal; all geometry covered by zone. Unknown score null, never zero. Route details/rain charts use the embedded cell snapshots actually used, not new weather calls; point-risk chart remains bound to its own RiskResponse.

RulesResponse.description: Exact configuration from validated rule bundle; no secrets; immutable version/checksum.

ProblemDetails.description: Same shape spec001; sanitized, never point/provider URI/image/body/SQL details.

capturedAt.description: Instant this immutable weather input was captured for the calculation; does not replace source dataTime/fetchedAt.

WeatherSnapshot.description: Full immutable weather input actually used, including source/timestamps, three hourly slots and simulation labels. Missing values stay null. Embedded value only: no server snapshot ID/store; weather-cell cache expiration cannot mutate this payload.

cell.description: Rounded 0.01-degree weather cell only, not an exact user GPS position.

RouteWeatherSnapshot.description: One cell input used by the route evaluation. Exactly one captured snapshot per cell per response, including unavailable weather; never refetched to explain an existing result.
